message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "#
# continuous-integration.yml
# Created by Felix Mau (https://felix.hamburg)
#

name: Continuous Integration
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  # Lint and Format
  # Ensures that the code adheres to the defined style guidelines.
  lint-and-format:
    runs-on: macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install SwiftFormat via Homebrew
        run: brew install swiftformat

      - name: Install SwiftLint via Homebrew
        run: brew install swiftlint

      - name: SwiftFormat
        run: make format-check

      - name: SwiftLint
        run: make lint

  # Tests
  # Ensures that the package compiles and that all tests pass, including code coverage reporting to Codecov.
  tests:
    runs-on: macos-26
    needs: lint-and-format
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Execute tests
        run: make test

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          fail_ci_if_error: true
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}

  # Build Example Application
  # Ensures that the package can be integrated into a real application, to catch any potential issues e.g. with access control.
  build-example-application:
    runs-on: macos-26
    needs: tests
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Build Example Application
        run: make build-example-application",
  "rationale": "P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is the best-supported fit. The measured experiment experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (evidence scope: measured_ci_workflow_on_fork) showed adding timeout-minutes cut median elapsed time by ~26.8%, and the pattern reports custom timeouts reduce runaway consumption (12.9% free / 8.1% paid VM time reduction). The repository's CI history shows successful runs complete in about 4-6 minutes total, so a 30-minute per-job timeout gives ample operational headroom and will not truncate valid runs while bounding stuck/runaway jobs. No matrix, schedule, or Bazel build exists, so fail-fast, schedule, and Bazel patterns do not apply. All existing steps, needs ordering, and required checks are preserved; no permissions, secrets, publishing, or new network access is added.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
